Original Articles
The Film

Downey Is Doom: The Comeback Nobody Predicted

Blockbuster Zone Original · By Sean O’Friel

Robert Downey Jr. built the Marvel era as Iron Man — the first face of the MCU, and the one fans said goodbye to in Avengers: Endgame. So when Marvel brought him back, it was never going to be as the hero. In Avengers: Doomsday he returns as Victor von Doom, the armored ruler of Latveria and the most dangerous mind in Marvel comics.

It is the boldest casting swing a studio has taken in years. Downey knows exactly what his face means to this audience — and now that meaning becomes the weapon. Every time Doom lifts his mask, the Avengers are not just fighting a villain; they are fighting the ghost of the man who saved them.

Marvel doubled down behind the camera, too. Anthony and Joe Russo, who directed Infinity War and Endgame, are back to steer the Avengers again. If anyone knows how to land a crossover of this size, it is them.

Cast & Story

What We Know About the Story So Far

Blockbuster Zone Original · By Sean O’Friel

Marvel is keeping the plot locked down, but the shape of it is clear. Doctor Doom makes his move, the Avengers assemble to stop him, and the fallout sets up Avengers: Secret Wars — already dated for December 17, 2027, exactly one year later.

The confirmed cast mixes eras in a way no Avengers film has before. Alongside Downey’s Doom, Pedro Pascal and Vanessa Kirby step in from Marvel’s First Family, the Fantastic Four — which tells you Doom’s story will not stay in one corner of the universe. This is the multiverse saga reaching its boiling point, with heroes from different worlds pulled into the same fight.

What to watch for: how Doom is introduced — as a threat the Avengers understand too late, if the comics are any guide — which heroes actually make the call to assemble, and the first real clues about how Secret Wars rebuilds everything in 2027.

Why It Matters

“Dunesday”: Why December 18 Is Bigger Than One Movie

Blockbuster Zone Original · By Sean O’Friel

On December 18, 2026, Avengers: Doomsday opens on the exact same day as Denis Villeneuve’s Dune: Part Three. Two event films, one Friday, and a fight for the same IMAX screens. Fans have already named it “Dunesday,” and it is shaping up to be the biggest single day at the movies in years.

That is why Doomsday sits at the top of this site. It is Marvel’s first Avengers film since Endgame, the return of its biggest star in the most unexpected role imaginable, and half of a double feature people will be telling stories about — whichever one they see first.

Our advice: book the big screen early, see both, and argue about the order afterwards. The countdown at the top of this page is running — we will be covering every trailer, casting surprise, and ticket milestone between now and December 18 right here.

Privacy Policy

Last updated November 6, 2026

Blockbuster Zone (BlockbusterZone.com) is owned and operated by Sean O’Friel of New York. This policy explains, in plain language, what information this site collects, what it does not collect, and how advertising — including Google AdSense — uses cookies on this site.

Information we collect

Blockbuster Zone has no user accounts, no sign-ups, no comment forms, and no checkout. We do not ask you for your name, address, or payment details in order to use the site, and we do not sell personal information.

Movie Night Points, your watched marks, star ratings, and short reviews are stored only in your own browser’s local storage on your device. They are never sent to us or anyone else, and clearing your browser data deletes them.

  • Email: If you email us, we receive your email address and the contents of your message. We use them only to read and reply to you.
  • Features in your browser: The movie search and the “My List” feature run entirely in your browser, on your device. Your My List picks are kept only in the page’s memory while the page is open. They are not saved, stored on a server, or sent anywhere, and they clear when you reload or leave the page.
  • Hosting logs: This site is hosted on GitHub Pages. Like any web host, GitHub may automatically log standard technical information (such as your IP address and browser type) when your browser requests a page. That processing is governed by GitHub’s own privacy policy, not by us.

Cookies and advertising

The site itself does not set cookies for its own features. Advertising is different:

  • House ads. The labeled ad slots currently promoting Blockbuster Zone itself are served as part of this page. They set no cookies and track nothing.
  • Google AdSense. This site is prepared to show ads through Google AdSense. When AdSense ads are served, third-party vendors, including Google, use cookies to serve ads based on your prior visits to this website and other websites on the internet.
  • Personalized ads. Google’s use of advertising cookies enables Google and its partners to serve ads to you based on your visits to this site and/or other sites. You can opt out of personalized advertising by visiting Google’s My Ad Center / Ads Settings, and you can opt out of some third-party vendors’ use of cookies for personalized advertising at aboutads.info. Turning off personalization does not remove ads; it makes them less tailored.
  • More from Google. Google explains how it uses information from sites that use its services in “How Google uses information from sites or apps that use our services” and in “How Google uses AdSense data.”
  • Your browser controls. You can block or delete cookies in your browser settings at any time. The site’s movie listings, search, and My List still work without advertising cookies.

External links and trailers

Pages on Blockbuster Zone link out to other sites — for example, YouTube for official trailers, and Entertainment Weekly, Rotten Tomatoes, Metacritic, and Box Office Mojo as sources. When you follow a link, that site’s own privacy policy applies. We do not control, and are not responsible for, the privacy practices of other sites.

How we use and share information

We use information only to operate and improve this site and to reply to emails. We do not sell or rent personal information. We may disclose information only if required by law, or to protect the rights and safety of this site and its visitors.

Your choices and rights

If you have emailed us, you may ask us to correct or delete your email and message by writing to us through the Contact Us page. Depending on where you live, you may also have rights to access, correct, or delete personal information and to opt out of personalized advertising, as described in the cookies section above.

Children’s privacy

Blockbuster Zone is a general-audience movie information site. It is not directed to children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13. If you believe a child has sent us personal information, please contact us and we will delete it.

Data retention and security

Emails are kept only for as long as they are needed to handle the conversation. No method of transmission or storage is completely secure, but we take reasonable care with the small amount of information this site handles.

Changes and contact

If this policy changes, the updated version will be posted on this page with a new date at the top. Questions about privacy can be sent through the Contact Us page or by email to sean.ofriel@aol.com.
